claims.text: The initial brittle MPEA has a coarse microstructure and may contain grain-boundary precipitates.
Low room-temperature tensile ductility in the initial state is associated with intergranular fracture.
The proposed processing schedule is a short anneal at about 900 °C for 5 min followed by aging at about 650 °C for 20 h.
The short high-temperature anneal generates a high dislocation density.
Rapid pipe diffusion causes δ-lamellae to nucleate at dislocation pile-ups within fcc grains.
Both δ-lamellae and γ″ particles nucleate specifically at intragranular dislocation pile-ups.
The stepwise treatment produces a homogeneous intragranular nanoscale-precipitate distribution rather than grain-boundary precipitation.
Moving precipitation from grain boundaries into grain interiors prevents intergranular embrittlement and permits high tensile ductility.
Synergistic strengthening by δ-lamellae and γ″ particles contributes approximately 1 GPa of strength without compromising ductility.
The processed alloy can reach a yield strength of approximately 2.0 GPa, compared with approximately 600 MPa in the as-cast state.
The processed alloy will have tensile elongation of at least 15% at room temperature.
The treatment can increase both yield strength and tensile ductility relative to the as-cast condition.
Conventional long-duration annealing or single-step aging typically causes precipitate coarsening or grain-boundary precipitation, producing low ductility despite possible strength gains.
Keeping oxygen below approximately 0.8 wt% prevents oxidation-induced embrittlement during processing.
The proposed mechanism is limited to alloy systems capable of forming the δ-lamellae/γ″ dual-precipitate structure through pipe diffusion.
The route may fail when the target precipitates are thermodynamically unstable or the matrix lacks sufficient dislocation density for pile-up nucleation.
Differences in diffusion coefficients or atomic sizes can make rapid pipe-diffusion kinetics difficult to control in other alloys.
The precipitate types and their synergistic effect may change when composition deviates substantially from the (W1.5Ni2.25Fe)95Ta5 system.

contradictions.description: The route is repeatedly called thermo-mechanical, but the specified intervention contains only annealing and aging and identifies no mechanical deformation step that would create the asserted dislocation density.
